newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks still quiet in London trading.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks still quiet in London trading.

text.p: Japanese stocks saw another quiet day in London dealing rooms on Tuesday, traders said, after Tokyo closed slightly lower in volatile trading.
The Nikkei 50 index of leading Japanese shares in London closed 7.15 points lower at 1,445.98, reflecting the Nikkei 225 index 44.13 point decline to end at 20,630.56.
Dealers said trading was quiet, and did not see Wednesday's volume any higher. "I may have blinked and missed it," said one.
Nomura dealer Jonathan Davis said, "We've seen buying in construction and domestic stocks such as Taisei and in banks like Mitsubishi and Sumitomo."
"The market tone still feels weaker in general," said Steve Crawley of Daiwa, adding that the market may open flat to a touch stonger in Toyko on Wednesday but could still drift off again.

One dealer, who reported selling in NEC and DKB bank, said that with profit taking in blue-chip companies, there had not been a great deal of reason to buy other stocks. He saw the Nikkei 225 index between 20,000 and 20,500 on Wednesday.
